question.text: A diverging lens with magnitude of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is placed at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from a converging lens of magnitude of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. A beam of parallel light falls on the diverging lens. The final image formed is:

options.text: Real and at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the convergent lens
Real and at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from convergent lens
Virtual and at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from convergent lens
Real and at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the divergent lens

solution.text:
Diverging lens forms the image at its focus. The image formed by diverging lens is the object for converging lens.

∴ Distance of the object from converging lens is 40 cm i.e., object is at double focal point.

∴ Image forms at double focal point on the other side of the lens.
1v-14=1f
1v-1-40=120
1v+140=120
1v=120-140=140
v=40
